name: Cleanup Corporation
court: inline advance court, main session 2026-08-03 (agent budget exhausted); generator was the mechanical EDINET shelf + FX overlay, so the generator-never-grades-itself invariant holds; no score reached 6 so no red team required
fx_context: USD/JPY 163.85 (Jul-23) -> 157.19 (Aug-2), +4.2% yen; IBKR IDEALPRO daily mid, tape-verified
verdict: WATCH 5/10 (was STARTER 6/10 pre-red-team) - fair price for a cheap asset with a guide-dependent catalyst; NOT a dislocation and NOT an FX trade
edge_class: RISK_PREMIUM (RP_FAIR) - not EDGE; the market is pricing today's earnings correctly and we are paying for an improvement we cannot yet verify
mode_b_first: Independent read: a JPY 134.5B domestic system-kitchen maker earning 2.9% EBIT is a low-return manufacturer, and 0.53x book is the market pricing exactly that. The value case cannot be 'cheap on book' — it must be a margin argument. Two things make it one: (1) FY3/27 guidance of revenue +5.6% with recurring profit +20.1% is management asserting operating leverage on its own; (2) the yen surge independently relieves imported input cost (steel, resin, appliances, fittings) — at a 2.9% margin, ~25% import content in COGS implies roughly +25% to EBIT for a 4.2% currency move. Those are the SAME lever from two directions, which is what makes this the one name where the FX story compounds a pre-existing thesis instead of substituting for one.

mode_a_verification.pb_strict_denominator: 0.53-0.57x on BOTH bases — survives the honest test (the shelf's loose denominator flattered six other names; this one does not need it)
mode_a_verification.capital_return: buyback WITH CANCELLATION executed 2026-02-05/06 — an action, not an intention; dividend raised 31->33 then held; TSE capital-policy disclosure updated 2025-11-20

the_bear_case_stated_properly: On JPY 134.5B of revenue a high-single-digit sales decline takes operating profit to roughly ZERO. That is the real risk of a 2.9% margin — the operating leverage cuts both ways, and Japanese housing starts are the swing factor. The register compounds it: ~46% sits with the Inoue founder vehicle (23.6%) plus supplier, dealer and employee associations, so no external party can force a return; it happens only if management chooses it. They have so far — that is evidence, not a guarantee.

fx_leverage_estimate.basis: assumed ~25% imported content of COGS at 70% COGS/revenue
fx_leverage_estimate.CONFIDENCE: LOW — import share is an ESTIMATE and is the single largest uncertainty; the FY3/27 Q1 tanshin segment/COGS detail is what confirms or kills it

entry_plan.rationale: lowered on the red team: 0.45-0.48x strict book, BELOW the 0.57x justified P/B at today's ROE, so the entry pays for the bear case rather than the base case. ~9-14% below the 906 spot.
entry_plan.sizing: 0.35% starter, scaling to 0.7% only after ONE clean quarter of the guided margin AND verification of the buyback size
entry_plan.gate: Q1 print 2026-08-07 first - do not pre-position

no further buyback or dividend action within 12 months of the Feb-2026 cancellation — the register argument dies without management choosing return
USD/JPY back above 162 (the FX leg of the thesis evaporates)

red_team_20260803.RT1_TAPE_KILLS_THE_DISLOCATION_FRAMING: the stock is UP 23.8% over twelve months and only 17.0% off its 52-week high (906 vs 1092). It ran 856 -> 1092 (+27.6%) into February 2026 and round-tripped. This is a name that ALREADY RE-RATED once - discovery_state is DISCOVERING, not undiscovered. I applied exactly this window-anchoring test to RIKEI and failed to apply it here. VERIFIED from IBKR daily bars.
red_team_20260803.RT2_THE_FX_LEG_IS_WEAKEST_WHERE_I_CLAIME: Cleanup builds STAINLESS-STEEL system kitchens. Japanese stainless is overwhelmingly DOMESTICALLY sourced (Nippon Steel, JFE, Nippon Yakin). My assumed ~25% imported COGS share was an unsourced guess and is probably too high; if the true share is 10%, the EBIT lift falls from ~+25% to ~+10%. The FX overlay may be a rounding error rather than a thesis leg. UNRESOLVED - needs the COGS/procurement disclosure.
red_team_20260803.RT3_WHERE_DOES_+5.6%_REVENUE_COME_FROM: Japanese housing starts are in structural demographic decline. The FY3/27 guide pairs revenue +5.6% with recurring profit +20.1% - the profit leverage is arithmetic IF the revenue lands, but the revenue assumption is the unexamined premise and no evidence for it was produced.
red_team_20260803.RT4_LOW_ROE_JUSTIFIES_LOW_BOOK: a 5.6-6.0% ROE business SHOULD trade below book; 0.53x is not obviously a discount to fair. Residual-income justified P/B at today's ROE is 0.57-0.66x depending on cost of equity - i.e. SPOT IS ROUGHLY FAIR on current earnings. The classic Japanese value trap shape.
red_team_20260803.RT5_BUYBACK_SIZE_UNVERIFIED: the Feb-2026 buyback-with-cancellation is cited as the key governance evidence but its YEN SIZE is unverified in our own intake. A token buyback proves nothing.
red_team_20260803.RT6_NO_EXTERNAL_LEVER: ~46% locked (Inoue vehicle 23.6% + supplier/dealer/employee associations). No activist can force anything.

blue_team_response_20260803.on_RT4_the_decisive_one: RT4 is right that spot is fair ON CURRENT EARNINGS - and that is precisely the asymmetry. At today's 6% ROE and a punitive 9% cost of equity, justified P/B is 0.57x against spot 0.53x. The market is pricing ZERO improvement. So the downside is largely in the price and the upside is entirely the guide landing. That is a real, if guide-dependent, asymmetry.
blue_team_response_20260803.on_RT1: CONCEDED and material. This is not a dislocation trade; it must stand as a fair-price-for-a-cheap-asset trade with a catalyst. It drops the score.
blue_team_response_20260803.on_RT2: CONCEDED - the FX leg is downgraded from a thesis pillar to an unquantified optionality. It should not be counted in the entry decision at all until the procurement disclosure is read.
blue_team_response_20260803.on_RT5: CONCEDED - verify the yen size before treating the buyback as governance evidence.
blue_team_response_20260803.net: the equity case survives on the strict-book discount + net cash floor + a management-asserted margin path. The FX case and the dislocation case do NOT survive.
